stories.headline: Sources: Steelers' contract philosophy led to Joey Porter Jr. trade
stories.summary: The Steelers' philosophy of avoiding second-year contract guarantees was a factor in their inability to reach a deal with Joey Porter Jr., sourced told NFL Network.
stories.body:
The Pittsburgh Steelers traded Joey Porter Jr. this past week, the final straw in a months-long standoff that resulted in the star cornerback playing Sunday for the Dallas Cowboys.

As for why the trade was necessary, sources pointed to the Steelers' general philosophy of avoiding second-year guarantees as the main reason.

In fact, Pittsburgh did offer Porter a contract that, with some work, could have been acceptable to keep him with the team. The Steelers offered Porter a contract deal that reached $28 million in average annual value -- a pitch that would've been the starting point for a deal to be consummated.

There was significant money guaranteed for injury, but not fully in the second year, as the Steelers held firm on a stance they have used often over the past few years. They are among the few teams to avoid guarantees past Year 1, joining Green Bay and Cincinnati among those the clubs that (mostly) take that stance.

But Steelers star pass rusher T.J. Watt received a second-year guarantee, as did wide receiver DK Metcalf, though his guarantee came in a trade. Declining to do so for Porter led to the contract impasse.

Porter, who now will play out his rookie deal in Dallas, wanted the security of a long-term contract rather than a large one-year payment. By the time this season started -- with Porter still ramping up after sitting out training camp -- he knew he would have been unlikely to play for Pittsburgh without a new contract.

Porter was, however, willing to do so for a fresh start with a new team. The Cowboys and Detroit Lions were the two biggest suitors, with Dallas getting him after the Steelers accepted a future second-round draft pick as part of the compensation. That was Pittsburgh's only serious trade offer.

Porter does not carry an injury designation into Sunday's game against the Houston Texans. Team executive vice president Stephen Jones said Friday that the Cowboys "actually think Joey Porter will get snaps."

stories.headline: Every team's odds to win the World Series: Dodgers still favorites as ALDS and NLDS begin
stories.summary: Every MLB team's odds to win the 2026 World Series as the playoffs begin.
stories.body:
As they were before the season, the Los Angeles Dodgers begin their postseason run as the consensus favorite to win the 2026 World Series. The Dodgers enter the playoffs at +200 to win the title -- not much shorter than the +230 odds they had coming into the 2026 season. The New York Yankees, another preseason favorite, are next at +500, tied with the Milwaukee Brewers, owners of MLB's best regular-season record.

The American League-leading Tampa Bay Rays round out the top four at +800. While bookmakers expected Los Angeles and New York to make it this far, they were more bearish on Milwaukee and Tampa Bay in the preseason, assigning them 35-1 and 80-1 championship odds, respectively.

The Atlanta Braves come in next at +850, followed by the Cleveland Guardians at 11-1. While neither of those teams have attracted too much action, some books have taken wagers and have World Series liability on the San Diego Padres, checking in at 11-1.

With the exception of the Brewers and Yankees at some books, the favorites aren't generally causing liability. However, there's one team every single bookmaker will be rooting against. The Chicago White Sox's run to the postseason has been nothing short of remarkable, given they entered the regular season with 500-1 World Series odds, tied for the worst in MLB. Between the long odds and the public's love of an underdog story fueling a betting frenzy, the liability piled up quickly across a variety of futures markets. Chicago enters the ALDS with 18-1 World Series odds, longest on the board.

Odds by DraftKings at time of publication.

stories.headline: Who most deserves the Ballon d'Or? Whittling down the 30-man short list
stories.summary: Kylian Mbappé, Lamine Yamal and Harry Kane are the three favorites to win the 2026 Ballon d'Or, but who actually deserves to win it?
stories.body:
For most of the past 15 years, there was really no point in campaigning for the men's Ballon d'Or -- it was going to the more obnoxiously successful of two men, Lionel Messi (eight-time winner) or Cristiano Ronaldo (five). Their personal -- and sometimes club -- rivalry defined the sport, to the point where even a rising star like Kylian Mbappé openly admitted he wasn't as good as them.

"It's not only me who knows that," he told writer Simon Kuper in "The Barcelona Complex." "Everyone knows it. If you tell yourself that you'll do better than them, it's beyond ego or determination -- it's lack of awareness. Those players are incomparable. They have broken all laws of statistics."

"I can't top them" probably isn't the healthiest thing in the world for a megastar to tell himself, but with Messi and Ronaldo finally having aged out of the competition -- Ronaldo hasn't finished in the top three of the voting in the 2020s, and Messi's final win came in 2023 -- now's the time to pounce.

Mbappé wants it. Lamine Yamal has said he wants it. Harry Kane thinks winning it would be "amazing." They're the three betting favorites for the award -- Kane's and Yamal's odds are both at +100 after a recent rise from Yamal, while Mbappé is at a longer +1000 -- but who actually deserves it?

After some late PR campaigns from players and clubs, voting for the award closed on Monday. It will go to the player who achieved the most between the beginning of the 2025-26 club season and the end of the 2026 FIFA World Cup. Thirty players were officially nominated, but based on who has won the award in the past, we can narrow the field pretty quickly.

- Ogden: Does Man City's guilty verdict impact Pep Guardiola's legacy?

- Marcotti: Hard to see how City recover from extraordinary guilty verdict

- Lindop: Liverpool can't afford to be without Isak, Gakpo in October

Eliminate anyone who played for Real Madrid last season

Eliminated: Jude Bellingham, Kylian Mbappé, Vinícius Júnior

I'm sorry, but we have to start here. The three players above are all dynamite, and two have come pretty close to winning the award already -- Mbappé was 192 points behind Messi in 2023, and Vinícius was only 41 points behind Rodri in 2024.

Mbappé is indeed No. 3 in the betting odds, and his scorpionlike quick strike capabilities might make him the most terrifying player in the world. At any point, it feels as if you could be about eight seconds from a Mbappé goal. He's great.

He has also been part of a terribly disappointing club team for two straight years. Since Mbappé joined Real Madrid, the only trophies they've won were the UEFA Super Cup and the FIFA Intercontinental Cup in 2024, trophies tied to accomplishments of the team before his arrival.

Real Madrid have finished behind Barcelona in both of Mbappé's seasons, and after winning the UEFA Champions League in the season before his arrival, they haven't made it past the quarterfinals with him. The Ballon d'Or isn't for club underachievers.

Mbappé is a delicious goal scorer, but his inability to even pretend to contribute in defense has held the team back significantly, especially combined with Vinícius' own refusal to do so. Mbappé did, however, have a fantastic World Cup, which is why he's No. 3 on the list -- he won the Golden Boot with 10 goals and became the competition's all-time leading scorer. But even there, his team lost to Yamal's Spain and Kane's England.

It would feel awfully strange if Mbappé retired without a Ballon d'Or, but he didn't earn it in 2025-26, nor did anyone else on a trophy-less Real Madrid team.

That cuts the list to 27 guys.

Actually, eliminate anyone who didn't win a trophy

Eliminated: Bruno Fernandes, Sadio Mané, Julián Quiñones

Technically, players have taken the Ballon d'Or after a trophy-less campaign, but it's rare. Kevin Keegan did it in 1978, back when it was called the "France Football European Footballer of the Year"; Figo did it in 2000 after leading Portugal to the Euro 2000 semis (and making a seismic move from Barcelona to Real Madrid that summer); and Ronaldo did it after scoring 55 goals in 2013. That's it. That's the list.

We watched Mané win a trophy back in the winter, when Senegal upset Morocco in a contentious Africa Cup of Nations final, but they were stripped of the award in March, so it was technically a trophy-free campaign for him. And though Quiñones scored four goals for Mexico at the World Cup (and 33 for Al Qadsiah in the Saudi Pro League) and Fernandes set a Premier League assists record, the bar for accomplishments in a World Cup year is too high. You need a trophy.

Now we're down to 24.

If you won only one trophy, you had better be an attacker

Eliminated: Marc Cucurella, Gabriel Magalhães, Declan Rice, William Saliba

Sorry, I don't make the rules. (I mean, I am kind of making the rules here, but they're based on history.) The one-trophy guys tend to be goal scorers -- Messi in 2019, the original Ronaldo in 2002, Roberto Baggio in 1993, Jean-Pierre Papin in 1990, Ruud Gullit in 1987, Michel Platini in 1983, Karl-Heinz Rumenigge in 1981, Keegan in 1979.

Arsenal won the Premier League with a fantastic core of midfielders such as Rice and defenders such as Gabriel and Saliba, and Cucurella, a fullback, was nearly error-free during Spain's World Cup run. But none of these guys score much.

That gets them eliminated, and it gets us down to 20 contenders.

When in doubt, eliminate anyone who had a disappointing World Cup (or didn't play in it)

Eliminated: Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, Marquinhos, Nuno Mendes, João Neves, Willian Pacho, Vitinha

In a World Cup year, the Ballon d'Or becomes extremely World Cup-centric. It's why Mbappé still has a prayer this year, and it's a main reason why Messi won in 2023 (after Argentina won 2022's winter World Cup), why Luka Modric won in 2018 (after Croatia's run to the final), why Manuel Neuer finished third in 2014 (after Germany's win), why Andres Iniesta and Xavi Hernandez finished second and third in 2010 (after Spain's win), why Fabio Cannavaro won in 2006 (after Italy's win), and on and on.

Unfortunately for a number of Paris Saint-Germain stars, a lack of World Cup success gets them eliminated. World Cup expansion means Georgia's Kvaratskhelia might have hope of playing there one day, but he didn't this summer, while Marquinhos was part of a disappointing Brazilian squad, Pacho's Ecuador bowed out in the round of 32, and Mendes, Neves and Vitinha were all part of a Portugal team that was supposed to contend and didn't. (I guess you could say that Ronaldo got four of his Portuguese teammates eliminated from this competition, too.)

This knocks our list all the way down to 14 remaining players.

You have to be the best player on your club team (or have a case that you are)

Eliminated: Luis Díaz, Pau Cubarsí, Fabián Ruiz, Ferran Torres, Dayot Upamecano

It seems fair, right? Cubarsí is a ridiculously sound center back, especially for a 19-year-old, and Upamecano is a major key to Bayern Munich's high-wire attacking style. Díaz proved his incredible "glue guy" characteristics when he left Liverpool for Bayern and the former fell apart, while the latter achieved a new level of attacking prowess. But few would make the case that these guys are better than Barça's Yamal or Raphinha, or Bayern's Kane or Michael Olise.

Torres, meanwhile, scored the World Cup-winning goal, but Barça let him leave for PSG. So, let's cross these five off our list. Now we're down to nine.

You should be among the top 3 in your position

Eliminated: Ousmane Dembélé, Lautaro Martínez, Lionel Messi

The final nine are all extremely accomplished and talented, so we have to raise the bar even higher. Using the summer's FC 100 voting, we can eliminate Martínez (No. 6 center forward), Messi (No. 5 wide forward) and Dembélé (No. 4 center forward). All three had excellent seasons and/or World Cup campaigns, but others have just been a little bit better in 2025-26. That gets us down to six.

Has anyone in your position ever won the Ballon d'Or?

Eliminated: Achraf Hakimi

Sometimes a non-attacker can transcend the counting stats and win the award. Rodri did, after all, in 2024 following the success of both Spain and Manchester City, and Modric won in 2018 after combining major club success (Real Madrid) with a World Cup run (Croatia). Cannavaro was among the best defenders of the 2000s and rode a World Cup title to victory over Italian teammate Gianluigi Buffon (also not a forward, obviously) in 2006. But no fullback has yet taken the award.

That's apparently a bridge too far. The closest thing was when a sweeper such as Matthias Sammer (1996) or Franz Beckenbauer (1972 and 1976) did the deed, but sweepers still aren't fullbacks, and that was three and five decades ago. Hakimi is the best fullback in the world and has been for a while, but he's not getting the nod.

We're down to five.

How was your club season?

Eliminated: Rodri

Watching Rodri in person at the World Cup was an incredible experience. He saw every potential counterattack against Spain developing 10 seconds in advance and was always in place to intercept the ball before it could start moving in the other direction. He was a timepiece, always keeping Spain from moving too slowly or too quickly. He probably benefited a bit from the slower pace of international play, but he was note-perfect during the tournament and deserved the Golden Ball award.

However, that all came on the heels of a club season in which he started only 17 league games for Manchester City while still trying to return to full form after his 2024 knee injury. The only reason he's on the list is because of the World Cup, and the four remaining guys on this list combined club success with great World Cup performances.

Your finalists

This process of elimination has left us with four potential winners, listed alphabetically:

Erling Haaland, 26, Manchester City/Norway

Relevant stats (club and country): 64 matches (2.19 PPG), 5,146 minutes, 58 goals, 11 assists from 45 chances created, World Cup quarterfinal, two trophies (FA Cup, Carabao Cup)

Harry Kane, 33, Bayern Munich/England

Relevant stats: 65 matches (2.60 PPG), 5,220 minutes, 73 goals, eight assists from 80 chances created, World Cup third place, three trophies (Bundesliga, German Cup, German Supercup)

Michael Olise, 24, Bayern Munich/France

Relevant stats: 69 matches (2.54 PPG), 5,314 minutes, 27 goals, 34 assists from 170 chances created, World Cup fourth place, three trophies (Bundesliga, German Cup, German Supercup)

Lamine Yamal, 19, Barcelona/Spain

Relevant stats: 57 matches (2.46 PPG), 4,574 minutes, 25 goals, 20 assists from 131 chances created, World Cup champion, three trophies (World Cup, LaLiga, Spanish Supercopa)

Actually, listing each player's relevant stats gives me an opportunity to address one of this year's primary Ballon d'Or controversies: the non-inclusion of Raphinha, Yamal's Barça teammate -- and maybe the hottest player in the world right now -- on the 30-man short list. Thirty players is a lot, and Raphinha had an obvious case, but in the time frame around which the award is based, he played only 40 matches and scored 21 goals with eight assists. He battled injuries and form, he barely played for Brazil at the World Cup (130 minutes, zero goals and assists), and he didn't really catch fire until the time frame ended. Consider him an early front-runner for 2027 (though I've already made my prediction in that race).

The betting odds tell us that two of these four players are far more likely to win than the other two, but all four have solid cases.

The case for Haaland

Haaland enjoyed another strong club season, scoring 38 goals with nine assists in all competitions. That almost sounds underwhelming by his standards, but it is still fantastic for someone in the best league in the club universe. Haaland might have enjoyed himself more than anyone else at the World Cup. His seven goals were the most by a World Cup debutant since 1974 (Poland's Grzegorz Lato), and he led Norway to its best-ever finish, a quarterfinal run that included a win over Brazil. (Naturally, he scored both of Norway's goals in that match.)

Haaland was also a bit of a pop culture phenomenon, buying cowboy hats, eating pastrami sandwiches and basically winning over every casual American sports fan. The World Cup belonged to him as much as anyone, and that usually earns you lots of Ballon d'Or votes. His case is likely dinged by both Manchester City's second-place finish to Arsenal in the Premier League and the dark clouds of the City scandal (which had nothing to do with him). But I was very surprised to see his odds for the award at only +4000, tied for eighth with Cubarsí, Dembélé, Olise and Bellingham. He'd be in my top five at worst.

The case for Olise

For my money, Olise is the best player in the world at the moment. That doesn't automatically mean he should win, and it's partially because of how he has started this new season. He already has eight goals and three assists in seven matches for Bayern, and when France needed a spark against Belgium this week in the UEFA Nations League, guess who sprang off the bench and immediately made the difference? But I was already starting to believe in his superiority last season.

Olise scored 22 goals with 26 assists in all competitions -- six to Kane -- for Bayern in 2025-26, a season in which he established himself as the best creator in the world. His touch and vision are sublime, and when it's time for him to do it himself, he's more than OK with doing that.

As with Haaland, Olise's odds are +4000, which is to say he's obviously not going to win it. But he'd be in my top three. He led the World Cup in assists with seven (no one else had more than four), and really, only a finishing slump held him back: He attempted 20 shots worth 2.5 xG, but none went in the net. But that's fine. For those of us in the Olise Is the Best in the World club, he can remain our little secret for a little while longer.

The case for Yamal

This is an award for 2025-26, but the case for Yamal almost has to start with Spain's current 40-match (and more than four-year) unbeaten streak. It correlates almost perfectly with the emergence of Yamal. He played 18 minutes in Spain's last defeat -- a 1-0 friendly loss to Colombia in March 2024 and his fifth appearance for Spain as a 16-year-old -- but during this unbeaten streak, he has started 28 of 40 matches. In this span, he's fourth on the team in minutes (2,305), third in goals (eight), second in shots on goal (36), progressive carries (320) and completed crosses (24) and first in assists (12), chances created (55), line-breaking passes received (297), ground duels won (184) and fouls suffered (44). Hell, he is also second in successful tackles (52) and third in ball recoveries (117).

Yamal wasn't even at full strength during the World Cup, having rushed back from injury, but he still played 615 of 750 minutes, and his mere presence out wide stretched and stressed defenses in ways that opened up opportunities for others. He was content playing more of a supporting role, refused to force the issue and lifted his second major international trophy before his 20th birthday.

Yamal has been the most valuable player on both the most successful international team of the 2020s and the team that has won the last two LaLiga crowns. And his magnetic personality, which comes through in virtually any interview, certainly doesn't hurt his Ballon d'Or cause. Putting together a career that rivals Messi's or Ronaldo's will take a level of longevity that we don't yet know he has, but at worst he's the second-most successful teenager ever behind Pele (who not only won a World Cup but also had two 50-goal campaigns).

The case for Kane

I'm finishing this list with Kane because, honestly, his is the easiest case to make. Yamal seems to be picking up momentum in the race, at least if betting odds are to be believed (and they frequently are), and if he wins it will be hard to say it was unjust. But look again at the stats above. Kane played eight more matches and over 600 more minutes than Yamal -- which is to say, he stayed healthier than a player 14 years his junior -- and he produced 81 combined goals and assists, a full 36 more than Yamal.

Does he play for one of the two most talented and prolific attacks in the world? Obviously. But so does Yamal!

Kane is England's all-time leading goal scorer and has the second-most goals in the history of the Premier League, but he achieved a new level of prowess in his 16th professional season. He scored over 60 club goals in all competitions for the first time, then he scored six goals in seven matches while leading England to the World Cup semifinals for the second time.

You could easily say that, when you're in doubt regarding whom to vote for, you should choose the older player who might not get another chance. But you don't even need to use that as a tiebreaker for Kane against Yamal because I don't think it's tied. He won nearly as much as Yamal at the World Cup, won every domestic trophy with Bayern and posted far superior statistics.

If I had a guess, I'd say Yamal wins at this point because of the late PR push. If I had a vote, however, I'd go with Kane.

stories.headline: Bahrain GP in Malaysia: Max Verstappen wins from pole as Kimi Antonelli extends title lead
stories.summary: Max Verstappen claimed his first victory of the season with a dominant drive in a heavily-delayed race at the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia.
stories.body:
Max Verstappen won a rain-hit Bahrain Grand Prix which was farcically delayed by one hour and 33 minutes after multiple cars broke down in the wet conditions before George Russell's outside world championship bid was derailed by a late engine failure.

Verstappen navigated his way through the chaos to claim his first triumph of the year. Kimi Antonelli took second with Lewis Hamilton completing a fine comeback drive from 18th to take the final spot on the podium. Russell had been running in third when he retired with just five laps left to leave his title dream all but over.

But the race at the Sepang International Circuit in Malaysia was overshadowed by embarrassing scenes when this season's new cars -- which had already faced stern criticism -- effectively failed to work in the wet.

Forty minutes after the initial getaway was pushed back following a deluge of rain, Formula 1 bosses had to abandon the start when number of drivers, including Verstappen and Hamilton, were struck by software gremlins -- directly linked to the controversial 50-50 split between combustion and battery power -- and could not get their cars to operate.

The grid limped back to the pit lane, and although the rain had long since stopped, a further 53 minutes passed before the green light was given by the sport's chiefs to try again. An explanation for the lengthy delay was not offered. And by now, the track was largely dry.

Two laps followed behind the Safety Car before a standing start. Verstappen slipped to third but cleared Antonelli after another Safety Car period on the 13th lap and took the chequered flag 2.3 seconds clear of the championship leader. Russell's failure to finish leaves him 84 points behind Antonelli with only seven scheduled races, and a possible 183 points remaining.

The rearranged round in Malaysia, because of the conflict in the Middle East, marked the first meaningful wet-weather running this year and it unravelled in spectacular fashion.

Pole-sitter Verstappen was the first to complain that he could not accelerate. That meant the following pack were virtually crawling around the Sepang circuit before Hamilton, second on the grid, then hit trouble in his Ferrari.

- Why is the Bahrain Grand Prix taking place in Malaysia, 4,000 miles away? F1's unusual race explained

- Bahrain GP in Malaysia: Max Verstappen takes first pole this season, Lewis Hamilton behind

Verstappen and Hamilton considered to be two of F1's great wet weather drivers, will start the race from first and second.

"I am pressing the throttle, and nothing is happening," he complained before stopping at the side of the track. And behind, a whole host of other drivers were also struggling to keep their engines running.

Attempting to explain the unprecedented scenes, Mercedes test driver Anthony Davidson said on Sky Sports: "What's effectively happening is if you are off throttle for too long, the turbo spools down and when the driver puts their foot back down, it uses all the engine juice.

"As soon as the battery goes flat, you are down to internal combustion engine power only. It's incredibly complicated and you fall into this horrible trap where the engine can't reaccelerate because you are being penalised by this regulation."

Verstappen, the leading critic of this season's rules, was eventually able to get up to speed. He laughed and shook his head upon seeing some of the cars parked at the side of the track.

"Look at this," he said over the radio.

Double world champion Fernando Alonso criticised the decision to abandon the start.

"Why did they put out the red flag?" he said. "This is racing."

The grid hobbled back to the pit lane and an almost one hour-long delay ensued despite no further rain, and the track initially declared fit for racing.

At 4.33 p.m. local time -- the fixture had been due to begin at 3 p.m. -- Verstappen peeled out of the pit lane. Red Bull and Mercedes elected for the intermediate tyres, while Ferrari and McLaren punted for slicks. It backfired for Ferrari and McLaren.

Russell leapt from seventh to second at the start with Antonelli assuming the lead, while Hamilton, desperately struggling on the dry tyres, fell back to as far as 18th and 80 seconds behind.

Valtteri Bottas beached his Cadillac on the ninth lap and a safety car was deployed. In came the leaders to change from inters to dry tyres, with Verstappen now ahead of Russell and in second. The Dutchman then mastered the restart to swat Antonelli aside. Russell also moved ahead of his teammate only for Antonelli to move back past for second on lap 21.

A lengthy Safety Car followed late in the fixture when Alex Albon stopped and his car, stuck in gear, could not be moved by the marshals. Then, Russell's afternoon, and quite possibly his title bid, came to an end as his power unit expired. But there were no such dramas for Verstappen, while Hamilton completed a fine afternoon by passing Hadjar at the end to take his first podium since the British Grand Prix in July.

stories.headline: Utah visits New York after Schmaltz's 2-goal game

stories.body:
Utah Mammoth (2-0, in the Central Division) vs. New York Rangers (2-1, in the Metropolitan Division)


New York; Sunday, 6 p.m. EDT


LINE: Rangers -135, Mammoth +111; over/under is 6


BOTTOM LINE: The Utah Mammoth visit the New York Rangers after Nick Schmaltz's two-goal game against the Columbus Blue Jackets in the Mammoth's 4-1 win.

stories.headline: USMNT's young stars shine to give Pochettino 'fantastic problem'
stories.summary: USMNT coach Mauricio Pochettino said that the number of players performing at a high level is "a fantastic problem to have" after teenagers Cavan Sullivan and Julian Hall propelled the USMNT to 3-0 win over rivals Mexico on Saturday.
stories.body:
GLENDALE, Ariz. -- United States men's national team coach Mauricio Pochettino said that the number of players performing at a high level is "a fantastic problem to have" after teenagers Cavan Sullivan and Julian Hall propelled the USMNT to 3-0 win over rivals Mexico on Saturday.

The U.S. endured a difficult first half, and scored completely against the run of play in the 28th minute when Hall converted from close range after Mexico keeper Raúl Rangel spilled Gio Reyna's low cross right in front of goal.

- Cavan Sullivan has arrived: U.S. phenom's goal caps a memorable win over Mexico

- Márquez bemoans 'terrible mistakes' as Mexico humbled by USMNT

- USMNT player ratings: Sullivan, Hall 9/10 in big win vs. Mexico

The USMNT began to make more headway in the second half, and doubled its lead in the 62nd minute when Sullivan intercepted a pass from Rangel, and chipped the ball into the net from 35 yards out. The match lost its edge when Mexico's Mateo Chávez was red carded in the 67th minute following a scrap with Sebastian Berhalter.

Malik Tillman finished off the scoring in the 84th minute, latching onto another wayward Mexico pass to firing into the net.

Hall, 18, is just the third USMNT player to score in his first three national team appearances, while 17-year-old Sullivan became the youngest scorer in USMNT history.

"I think it's a fantastic problem for us," Pochettino said about the performances of his team's young players. "I think we will take the right decision in the right moment, but I think it's a very good problem to see.

"Now it's not a moment at all, but yes, we appreciate that situation and of course hope that we will be in that situation that young players perform in the way that they deserve to be with us."

Pochettino also pronounced himself pleased with the way his side weathered Mexico's early pressure.

"I think that this, overall, was a great opportunity to discover ourself, to see ourselves in a difficult game with a very good team. Again, Mexico is a great team," Pochettino said.

"Yes, I think two different maybe halves. The first half I think Mexico started really well. They forced us to play back. We never connected. We were losing all the duels. And then we start to grow after 15, 20 minutes. And I think it was a good lesson the first half because it was the sense of work all together, suffer together even when you are not playing well in the way that you plan to play."

But Pochettino couldn't help but admire the performance of Sullivan, who impressed with his work on both sides the ball.

"I think he's a talented player with enormous quality, but with a very good balance, in possession and out of possession," Pochettino said about Sullivan. "He's a fighter, he's a warrior. It's difficult to find this type of player with a tremendous quality.

"And then I think Cavan showed in possession with the ball on the field [and] when he need to be chasing people and recover the ball. That is my impression after maybe three weeks together. And that is unbelievable, to have a player like this. I think it's a fantastic news for USA. Hope that continues in that way."

Pochettino was careful to laud Sullivan's young teammates as well, who have largely impressed during this window.

"It's a big moment because we need to be right with them," Pochettino said about the win, and the path forward. "We need to protect them. We need to support them. Our responsibility now is that this group of talented players grow in the right direction."

stories.headline: AFL: Heavyweight trades loom large over AFL free agency period
stories.summary: Essendon and Hawthorn's jostling over Zach Merrett and deals for free agents Zak Butters and Ben King will headline another bumper trade and free agency period.
stories.body:
Essendon and Hawthorn's jostling over Zach Merrett and deals for free agents Zak Butters and Ben King will headline another bumper AFL trade and free agency period.

Brisbane's dual Brownlow medallist Lachie Neale and GWS captain Toby Greene respectively strolled to Collingwood and Geelong after free agency opened on Friday, courtesy of their unrestricted status.

Port Adelaide superstar Butters and Gold Coast key forward King face a longer wait as restricted free agents.

The Power can match any bid for 26-year-old Butters, who nominated the Western Bulldogs as his preferred destination over Geelong, and will want more than the first-round compensation they would otherwise garner.

As league-wide haggling ramps up when the trade period opens on Monday, the Bulldogs may well have to get creative at the negotiating table to satisfy Port.

Gold Coast have similarly canvassed matching a rival bid for King when Hawthorn officially come knocking for the Victorian spearhead.

A bid on Butters or King would generate band one compensation, currently valued at pick five for Port and pick seven for Gold Coast.

Complicating matters, Hawthorn is making another dash at Merrett after Essendon sensationally rejected offers for the gun midfielder in 2025.

The Hawks hold a respectable draft hand, with four draft picks between 15 and 33 on top of future first-round selections in 2027 and 2028.

Merrett, who turned 31 on Saturday, is entering the final year of his Bombers contract and clinched a seventh club best and fairest award after a disastrous two-win season.

With Butters and Merrett spurning Geelong's advances, the Cats have shifted their focus to injury-plagued Essendon defender Jordan Ridley, contracted until 2029, and St Kilda ruckman Rowan Marshall.

St Kilda asked for a player in exchange for Marshall after the contracted 30-year-old requested a trade away to the Cattery for a second straight season.

The Cats were not keen to entertain giving up young half-back Lawson Humphries but talks for Marshall remain ongoing.

In other wheelings and dealings, Gold Coast is expected to trade a late pick for Collingwood veteran Scott Pendlebury if King walks as a restricted free agent so as not to dilute their compensation pick.

Dumped GWS forward and 2024 Coleman medallist Jesse Hogan is also expected to join Collingwood for a late pick rather than waiting for delisted free agency.

Carlton are reportedly trying to prise contracted half-back Lachie Whitfield out of GWS, while trade speculation surrounds Nick Blakey after he and four other Sydney Swans players were banned on the eve of the finals.

Brisbane premiership winger Sam Marshall is eyeing a trade to St Kilda, Luke Pedlar wants a rare switch from Adelaide to Port Adelaide, and Geelong midfielder Jack Bowes is trying to get to Essendon.

Jack Viney, Melbourne's 2021 premiership vice-captain, on Thursday said a deal would be done after he met with West Coast.

Demons coach Steven King told the 32-year-old midfielder he was likely to be on the outer next season despite having two years remaining on his contract.

The free agency period ends on Friday, while the trade window wraps up on October 14.

stories.headline: UFC 332 takeaways: Talbott, Silva validate their top billing
stories.summary: Payton Talbott finished another former champion in Deiveson Figueiredo on a night full of knockouts at UFC 332.
stories.body:
The options were plenty for performance bonuses after UFC 332 in Salt Lake City. The fight card set a UFC record for knockouts with 11, and nine came in the first round. The most resounding KO went to men's bantamweight Payton Talbott in the co-main event. He came out strong, sending former champion Deiveson Figueiredo to the canvas twice before finishing him a little over two minutes into the fight. The win is Talbott's second in a row over a former champion and likely means big things ahead for him, but the loss for Figueiredo doesn't do anything to minimize his legacy in the UFC.

The main event, which received prefight chatter over whether it was worthy of a headlining slot, was high energy but mostly one-sided. Natalia Silva, the No. 1 women's flyweight contender, earned her first UFC championship with a unanimous decision over Wang Cong. The 29-year-old joins men's flyweight Joshua Van as the only UFC champions under 30.

Was the main event criticism validated?
The UFC took heat on social media for booking Silva vs. Wang in a main event on a numbered card. Silva was at the front of a long line of women's flyweight title contenders, no question, but it's fair to say Wang, unranked by ESPN and outside the top five in the UFC's own rankings, jumped the queue.

But while I'm on board with a lot of the criticism the UFC receives for its matchmaking, especially at a championship level, I understand what the fight promotion was going for in this case: The UFC was trying to set up a couple of possible storylines involving Valentina Shevchenko, who vacated the women's flyweight title to make the Silva-Wang title fight a possibility after suffering an undisclosed injury that will sideline her for "up to one year."

Why Wang? She might not have an extensive UFC résumé, but she beat Shevchenko in a kickboxing match in 2015. Their history is not unlike that of Alex Pereira and Israel Adesanya, who met twice in kickboxing, with Pereira winning both and knocking out Adesanya in one of those fights. It provided a setup for their UFC rivalry.

A Wang vs. Shevchenko angle became moot, as things turned out, because Silva was too much for the Chinese fighter to handle. Wang came in with a 10-1 MMA record, but she had zero fights against top-10 flyweights, and it showed. Silva, by contrast, came in having defeated former UFC champions (Jessica Andrade, Alexa Grasso and Rose Namajunas) in each of her past three fights.

Silva was too fast, too elusive and too precise with her punches and kicks. Wang had no answers, looked lost and couldn't get her offense going until the fifth round, when it was too late. Not to vindicate the prefight matchmaking criticism, but this sure was a lopsided and not-so-fiery bout, one that got booed by a crowd that had been treated to a UFC-record 11 knockouts on the night.

So now the 125-pound division is left with the Silva vs. Shevchenko storyline we were expecting to see before Shevchenko was injured. It will be interesting to see how Silva's speed holds up when she meets her predecessor with the belt, and how differently she'll fight when up against an opponent with a strong grappling game. Oddly, that wasn't even addressed in Silva's postfight interview in the cage. Shevchenko's name wasn't even mentioned. Now, that is a UFC decision worth questioning. -- Jeff Wagenheim

Quick thanks to Figueiredo

MMA loves to move quickly, and it's ready to move very fast with Talbott. Talbott is everything MMA could want in a prospect, and his future is very bright.

So before we all take off on the Talbott train (as we inevitably will), let's take a moment to shout out one of the most exciting flyweights of all time, Figueiredo.

Let's be honest, Figueiredo was always a borrowed bantamweight. He struggled to make 125 pounds, and most of the sport was happy to see him ditch the weight cut in 2023, but he was also undersized at 135.

It's easy to forget now, as UFC men's flyweight champion Van has taken the sport by storm -- but the flyweight division was still in a precarious position when Figueiredo made his mark in 2020. Henry Cejudo saved the division by knocking out TJ Dillashaw in 2018, but then eventually vacated a weight class the UFC seriously considered shutting down. Figueiredo picked up where Cejudo left off, saving the division with his one-punch knockout power and (frankly) villain charisma. He played the role of "bad guy" in his back-to-back fights against Joseph Benavidez in 2020, as well as his four-fight rivalry with Brandon Moreno.

It was inevitable when he moved up in weight, but for a three-year period, Figueiredo was the exact figure the flyweight division needed. The 38-year-old's career is undoubtedly coming to an end soon, but Figueiredo was not just a terrific fighter and champion in his prime, he will forever be remembered as a significant hero of flyweight MMA. -- Brett Okamoto

stories.headline: Lakers' Ziaire Williams proposes to longtime girlfriend at Bruno Mars tour
stories.summary: The singer complemented the proposal during his second of five Inglewood shows.
stories.body:
Pop superstar Bruno Mars knows how to put on a good show. But on Friday night, one audience member seemed to steal the show from the 16-time Grammy winner.

As Mars performed "Marry You" during his second night of five in Inglewood, California, for "The Romantic Tour," Los Angeles Lakers forward Ziaire Williams found the perfect moment to make a promise for forever.

On the floor level of SoFi Stadium, Williams got down on bended knee as Mars sang the words "I think I wanna marry you," lining up his question -- "Will you marry me?" -- with the lyrics.

As Williams proposed to his teary-eyed girlfriend, model Paris Timan, Mars blended his singing with his excitement, crooning, "Please say I do I do I do."

After Timan -- who seemed to be in shock -- said yes, Mars continued singing through the song's conclusion while the couple shared a hug as the audience erupted in cheers.

Timan will be part of two new beginnings for Williams. In July, the 25-year-old signed a one-year, $3 million deal with the Lakers after a 2025-26 season in which he posted 10.2 points and 2.4 rebounds per game in 54 games with the Brooklyn Nets.

And the next part? Planning the rest of their lives together. Nothing screams "fairy tale" more than a proposal to a Mars love song.

stories.headline: NRL Grand Final: Teams, line-ups, tips, odds, everything you need to know for the weekend
stories.summary: Here we finally are, the 2026 NRL Grand Final where the red, white and blue Sydney Roosters will battle it out with the red, white and slightly different blue Newcastle Knights for premiership glory.
stories.body:
Here we finally are, the 2026 NRL Grand Final, where the red, white and blue Sydney Roosters will battle it out with the red, white and slightly different blue Newcastle Knights for premiership glory. Can last year's wooden spooners extend the Justin Holbrook-inspired fairytale for one more week? Will the seasoned Roosters be too good?

Let's not forget that the Knights won their only two premierships as underdogs against the Sea Eagles in 1997 and Eels in 2001. Beware tippers, fans and experts alike; you should never tell a Novocastrian that they can't do something.

Good luck with your tips.

Sunday, October 4
Sydney Roosters vs. Newcastle Knights
Accor Stadium, 7:30pm (AEDT)
Roosters: 1. James Tedesco 2. Daniel Tupou 3. Billy Smith 4. Robert Toia 5. Mark Nawaqanitawase 6. Daly Cherry-Evans 7. Sam Walker 8. Naufahu Whyte 9. Reece Robson 10. Lindsay Collins 11. Salesi Foketi 12. Siua Wong 13. Victor Radley Bench:15. Angus Crichton 16. Nat Butcher 17. Spencer Leniu 18. Hugo Savala 19. Cody Ramsey 20. Benaiah Ioelu

- Enter your NRL Tipping Competition tips today with footytips.com.au

Knights: 1. Kalyn Ponga 2. Dominic Young 3. Dane Gagai 4. Bradman Best 5. Greg Marzhew 6. Fletcher Sharpe 7. Sandon Smith 8. Tyson Frizell 19. Thomas Cant 10. Cody Hopwood 11. Jermaine McEwen 12. Francis Manuleleua 13. Mathew Croker Bench: 14. Harrison Graham 15. Lachlan Crouch 16. Pasami Saulo 17. Dylan Lucas 18. Fletcher Hunt 21. Diesel Hagan

Officials

Referee: Adam Gee Touchies: Tyson Brough, Phil Henderson

Bunker: Chris Butler

Prediction: The Roosters came out against the Dolphins last weekend with a fire lit inside each and every player. They looked at the Dolphins' tendency to start slowly and doubled down on the early pressure and the ferocity of their defence. The Dolphins usually ride out the initial forward battering and points conceded, before storming home through their superior backline. Last weekend, the Roosters hit them with such sustained intensity that they had nothing left in the tank after the break. The Dolphins' back three were swarmed upon every time they tried to work their team into decent field position.

With the ball, the Roosters welcomed back Sam Walker, his steady hand and creativity adding just the ingredient they needed to pile on the points. James Tedesco contributed without playing the house down, centres Robert Toia and Billy Smith were hard to stop and even harder to get past and wingers Daniel Tupou and Mark Nawaqanitawase were at their brilliant best. But the game, as all the big ones are, was won in the forwards where Victor Radley was at his destructive best working well with Naufahu Whyte, Lindsay Collins, Salesi Foketi and Siua Wong. When rested, the effort didn't dip at all with Angus Crichton and Nat Butcher lined up to continue the dominance. They will be looking to play a similar game against the Knights in the big dance.

The Knights pulled off a miraculous victory over the Panthers after being reduced to 12 players, 35 minutes into the game. They have been playing with a never-say-die attitude all season, with a defence that never quits and an attack willing to throw the ball around at any point on the field. They have a very mobile team, a pack of no-frills forwards led by the inspirational Tyson Frizell who work their butts off for each other and enough flair and speed in the backs to cause headaches for a defence from all parts of the ground.

The Knights have a powerful set of wingers in Dom Young and Greg Marzhew, experience, explosive skill and guile in centres Dane Gagai and Bradman Best and an every-improving halves pairing in Fletcher Sharpe and Sandon Smith. At fullback is Kalyn Ponga, on his day one of the best players in the league, who comes off a brilliant performance against the Panthers.

They have been defying the naysayers all season and are playing with an unmatched level of confidence. The whole of the Hunter Valley is behind them and a victory here would mean so much to the entire region. The majority of neutral fans will also be cheering for an upset in this one and Accor Stadium will light up if they manage to knock over the cocky Roosters.

They will have to contain the Roosters forwards, nullify the attack of Sam Walker, Daly Cherry Evans and James Tedesco and have everything go their way on the day. I am going to assist the Knights by saying I can't see them winning this. I was wrong last week, Knights fans will be hoping that I am wrong once more.

Tip: Roosters by 8

stories.headline: How to bet Lions-Panthers on 'SNF': Analysis, tips and top prop plays
stories.summary: Odds, bets and analysis to help you bet Lions-Panthers on "Sunday Night Football."
stories.body:
The Detroit Lions enter as the favorite on the road against the Carolina Panthers on "Sunday Night Football." The 2-1 Lions are coming off a 31-24 win over the New York Jets, while the Panthers fell to 1-2 after a 21-18 loss to the Cleveland Browns.

Detroit has balance, with the ability to attack Carolina on the ground and through the air, forcing a depleted defense to choose where to commit help. Jahmyr Gibbs threatens the edges and makes defenders miss, while Amon-Ra St. Brown gives Jared Goff a reliable answer underneath. With cornerbacks Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson sidelined, Carolina has fewer options for covering Detroit's receivers without sacrificing support against the run.

The Panthers do have a counter: they disguise their safety looks after the snap and defend play action well, potentially complicating Goff's reads when he turns his back to the defense. Carolina's offense faces a different problem. Bryce Young has shown he can beat man coverage, but protection breakdowns undermine those opportunities. Detroit's pressure can exploit an injured offensive line.

If Young gets time, however, the Lions' vulnerable secondary offers openings for Tetairoa McMillan and Darren Waller, particularly with the Panthers likely leaning on quick throws to avoid sacks.

Betting outlook
I prefer Detroit -3.5 because Carolina's injuries make it difficult to see the Panthers consistently trading scores. Detroit has scored 31 points in every game, its offense still producing despite inconsistencies. Carolina could produce offensively and still fall short of covering if its depleted defense can't get enough stops.

Over 50.5 is a tougher commitment. Even if Detroit reaches its average again, Carolina needs at least 20 to get us there. Waller offers a promising outlet at tight end against a Lions defense that has allowed six touchdowns to the position, but Young's protection (or lack of) makes sustained scoring less dependable.

Sacks could kill possessions before that matchup advantage translates into points. The Panthers' aggressive passing approach keeps the over viable, especially if they spend the second half chasing the Lions. But that comeback production is something I'm less willing to count on.

The spread and total don't have a clear edge on either side.

Notable player props, bets

Note: Odds by DraftKings and subject to change.

Jahmyr Gibbs 140+ rushing and receiving yards (-112)

Gibbs' workload travels across game scripts. Detroit can feed him carries while leading or find him through the air if Carolina stays close. The Panthers have allowed a league-worst 580 rushing yards on 5.7 yards per carry. That gives Gibbs room to produce on the ground, while his seven targets per game gives this wager another path beyond rushing production. We're backing a heavy workload against a defense struggling to stop the run.

Darren Waller Anytime TD +260

Liz Loza: Waller has emerged as a legitimate part of the Panthers' offense. Not only has his snap share increased each week (34% to 43% to 49%), but his eight targets led the team last Sunday. He's also been active in the red area, recording two end zone looks and hauling in two touchdowns over three contests. He has a good shot at hitting pay dirt again in Week 4 versus the Lions, as six different tight ends have recorded a TD when facing Detroit.

stories.headline: Transfer rumors, news: Arsenal among clubs chasing winger Yildiz
stories.summary: Arsenal, Real Madrid and Bayern Munich are all chasing Juventus winger Kenan Yildiz. Transfer Talk has the latest.
stories.body:
Arsenal, Real Madrid and Bayern Munich are all chasing Juventus winger Kenan Yildiz. Plus, could Endrick leave Real Madrid for AC Milan?

Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Real Madrid are pushing for Kenan Yildiz with Arsenal and Bayern Munich also looking at the Juventus winger, reports Corriere dello Sport. Juve have been demanding at least €100 million for the 21-year-old for a year, but Madrid are reigniting their interest in him with the view to a move in the summer. They would want to pit him and Vinícius Júnior against each other, while Arsenal see the Turkiye international as the answer to their lack of options on the left and Bayern have been watching him from afar since his departure.

- AC Milan are planning to make another attempt to sign Real Madrid striker Endrick after being unable to bring him in during the summer, reports La Gazzetta dello Sport. Madrid boss Jose Mourinho had initially refused to let the 20-year-old leave, but he has made just one substitute appearance this season that lasted four minutes. Milan's main competition from within Italy for the Brazil international is Roma, while Aston Villa were also unsuccessful in their efforts to bring him in last summer.

- Barcelona are willing to let Alejandro Balde leave on loan in January with Manchester United among the clubs interested in the left-back, according to TEAMtalk. The 22-year-old has fallen down the pecking order in Hansi Flick's squad and has only got onto the pitch once so far this season, playing the last 12 minutes in a 7-2 win over Racing Santander. The Spaniard's camp and intermediaries are already working hard to find a solution for him, while the Blaugrana could look to bring in a new left-back in 2027.

- Liverpool center back Giovanni Leoni is the latest name La Gazzetta dello Sport have linked with Juventus, as I Bianconeri aim to introduce young Italian talent to their squad. The Serie A side have turned their attention away from the likes of Arsenal's Riccardo Calafiori and Chelsea's Marco Palestra, who are now seen as unattainable, and had already made enquiries about a loan for Leoni in recent months. Liverpool haven't opened the door to the 19-year-old leaving, but Juventus aren't giving up on him.

- Barcelona are interested in 18-year-old FC Twente center back Ruud Nijstad, reports transfer journalist Fabrizio Romano. They are monitoring the young Dutchman, having already made contact about him in August but ultimately being told that a transfer wasn't possible as Twente wanted him to be a key player for them. More clubs are showing an interest in Nijstad and have started travelling to scout him.

- Real Madrid are among the clubs who could move to sign Manchester United attacker JJ Gabriel, according to Spanish newspaper AS. Various clubs across Europe are looking at the 15-year-old after it was made clear that he wants to leave the Red Devils and requested a transfer. Bayern Munich have emerged as major rivals for his signature and Barcelona have gained momentum in recent days. Man United have leaked that they will take legal action against any club that negotiates with Gabriel.

Other rumors
- Arsenal, Barcelona, AC Milan, and Juventus all want to sign 15-year-old Borussia Dortmund midfielder Justin Ejodamen. (TEAMtalk)

- Tottenham Hotspur have no interest in letting Micky van de Ven leave as Liverpool prepare to move for the centre-back next year. (Football Insider)

- Manchester United, Arsenal, and Chelsea are making regular checks on Freiburg striker Igor Matanovic. (Caught Offside)

- Newcastle United are open to letting 27-year-old midfielder Joe Willock leave in January. (Football Insider)

- Leeds United aren't planning on letting Dan James leave, but the 28-year-old could look to depart in January. (Football Insider)

- Roma are planning a contract extension for Mario Hermoso. (Nicolo Schira)

stories.headline: Bahrain GP in Malaysia: George Russell suffers major title blow after race retirement
stories.summary: George Russell's title chances took a critical blow at the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia after he retired from the race under a Safety Car with five laps remaining.
stories.body:
George Russell's title chances took a critical blow at the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia after he retired from the race under a Safety Car with five laps remaining.

Russell was running in third place, one position behind teammate and title rival Kimi Antonelli, when his car suffered an apparent power unit failure and pulled to the side of the track.

Racing had been suspended under a Safety Car after Alex Albon's Williams suffered a gearbox problem, leading to an extended caution period as marshals struggled to move it behind a barrier.

With racing due to resume on the next lap, Russell's car pulled to a halt at the end of the pit straight, with the British driver holding his head in his hands in the cockpit.

Russell, who went into Sunday's race 66 points behind Antonelli, had passed his teammate following an earlier Safety Car, only to lose the position again on lap 21 and return to third place.

Russell's chances of beating Antonelli to the title over the remaining races already looked slim before the retirement, but now appear close to zero.

stories.headline: LeBron James calls scrimmage 'great first step' for new-look 76ers
stories.summary: Throngs of fans waited in lines more than 10-deep to watch LeBron James, Jaylen Brown and the rest of the 76ers take part in Saturday's scrimmage.
stories.body:
PHILADELPHIA -- It might have been the basketball equivalent of a dress rehearsal, but the 76ers' intrasquad scrimmage Saturday certainly gave a promising glimpse of what could be in store when the curtain actually comes up for the 2026-27 NBA season.

Philadelphia hosted its annual Blue-White game in front of approximately 10,000 fans at Xfinity Mobile Arena, moving the exhibition from their G League affiliate's home in Delaware to accommodate the added interest in the new-look team.

While throngs of fans waited in lines more than 10-deep in the atrium an hour before the noon start, there was plenty of on-court action from LeBron James, Jaylen Brown & Co. to enjoy as soon as the scrimmage started.

"To be able to take what we've done on the practice floor, bring it to a game floor situation around our fans ... it was a great first step in the direction we're trying to go," James said.

Longtime Sixers public address announcer Matt Cord, who had retired before deciding to come back once Philadelphia had its historic summer, announced the starters for the Blue team.

First Tyrese Maxey, then VJ Edgecombe, then Brown, then James and then the man in the middle who has been with the franchise for 13 years.

"7-2 from Cameroon, No. 21, Joel 'The Processsss' Embiiddddd!" Cord bellowed.

"It doesn't matter who gets announced first, last, second, third," Embiid said.

But the cheers that followed every name did mean something to him.

"We love the fans," Embiid said. "We want them, and we need them to be part of this. I mentioned it at media day: It's already hard enough to win as a group that gets together for the first year. So we're going to need all we can, whether it's from everybody in this building, the fans, the outside people, we're going to need to get together. We're going to need all the support possible."

The Sixers didn't keep an official box score, but the stats mattered far less than some of the sequences that showed the early chemistry that is developing after a week of training camp, including James finding a trailing Embiid for an above-the-break 3.

"Guys are going to use their speed against people and try to score a quick basket, and if we don't have anything, I'm the trail guy," Embiid said matter-of-factly.

Both Maxey and Kentavious Caldwell-Pope delivered feeds to James for alley-oop dunks that the 41-year-old star finished with ease. Embiid got his 7-foot frame to lift high enough to both block springy second-year guard Edgecombe and have a dunk of his own.

"Pretty good, not bad," a noticeably slimmed-down Embiid said when asked how he felt physically compared to last season. Then he showed his sense of humor is as strong as ever.

"That's probably the last dunk of my career," Embiid said with a smirk.

While James has had only four official Sixers practices, plus the scrimmage, it was enough for him to conclude that Embiid is a different player than the guy he won a gold medal with at the Paris Olympics two summers ago.

"The difference between '24 and now, he's just so much more healthier," James said. "He hasn't missed a practice. He's been in damn near everything that we've done. Pretty much. They've had to sit him out at times, even when he wanted to keep going. ... So it's been good. Actually, great."

Philadelphia limited the scrimmage to three 10-minute quarters but started each period with the scoreboard set to 80-80 to simulate an end-of-game scenario.

Sixers coach Nick Nurse, who thanked the crowd for its support after the scrimmage, is giving the team the day off Sunday before it opens its four-game preseason slate by hosting the New York Knicks on Monday.

"It will be good to get out there with some of our guys to just get a rhythm," James said of the preseason schedule. "At the same time, also not overdo it, because we're putting a lot into our practices right now, fine-tuning what we want to do once the [regular-season] games come, but there'll be opportunities when we get out there in the preseason."

stories.headline: Fever's Mitchell says she'll be 'selfish' with free agency call
stories.summary: Retaining unrestricted free agent Kelsey Mitchell is a top offseason priority for the Fever, according to general manager Amber Cox and coach Stephanie White.
stories.body:
INDIANAPOLIS -- Retaining unrestricted free agent Kelsey Mitchell is a top offseason priority for the Indiana Fever, both general manager Amber Cox and coach Stephanie White acknowledged Saturday morning. The four-time All-Star had a career year in which she set the WNBA single-season records for points scored and 3-point field goals made.

Mitchell, however, said she will be "selfish" with her decision-making.

"I have to be selfish," Mitchell said during her end-of-season media session. "I think that's where I am in my career ... what I probably need and what's probably best for me. So I have to be selfish in that room.

"But I think, ultimately, being on the Fever and being a part of an organization that does come with a lot of ups and downs, what factors in and what is important for me is, obviously, having a good chemistry on and off the floor. I've only been with one team my entire career, so it's all kind of like figuring this out. It's hard, man."

Mitchell ranked No. 2 in the league with a career-high 24.7 points per game while shooting 50.9% from the field and 45.0% from behind the arc. She is expected to receive a high number of MVP votes and be named all-WNBA first team for the second season in a row.

Cox said the goal is to have Mitchell retire in a Fever uniform.

"She has a lot of equity in this franchise and has put in a lot of time," Cox said. "She's meant so much to us and has, obviously, had, arguably, the best season in the history of our league in terms of being a scoring guard. The numbers she put up were just spectacular, and you hear night in and night out from players across this league -- the hardest person to guard in this league is Kelsey Mitchell.

"When you put her in the backcourt with Caitlin [Clark] ... historic in terms of what they were able to do, and we hope we have the opportunity to build upon that."

Mitchell and Clark became the highest-scoring duo in WNBA history as they led highest-scoring offense in league history. The 30-year-old Mitchell also set the league record for the most consecutive games scoring 20-plus points (27). She received the core designation from the team the past two seasons and cannot receive it again.

Being in a backcourt with Clark is something Mitchell values, she explained, and that will be important in her decision-making. But Mitchell added that playing in Indiana and with Clark can be difficult due to the vitriol from some fans.

"It's a lot to hash out," Mitchell said. "I just think that I've got to be selfish about where my career is going a little bit in terms of some of the things, as I get older, what's important for me, whether it be winning, whether it be my own individual success. I worked my tail off to be here, though, man. So whatever I do, it's gonna come from a selfish standpoint. I'll be honest about that."

A more difficult decision for the Fever lies with unrestricted free agent Sophie Cunningham. The eight-year veteran had a strong start to the season and was even considered a Sixth Player of the Year candidate after the first two months, but she cooled down the stretch. She finished with 7.9 points per game, her lowest scoring average since 2023.

Controversy also swirled around Cunningham on multiple occasions for her comments to ESPN regarding transgender athletes, a kerfuffle with DiJonai Carrington and a finger-pointing incident with DeWanna Bonner. Cunningham is outspoken on social media and her podcast. Protesters and supporters began to show up outside arenas after Cunningham's comments regarding transgender athletes in women's sports.

Cox said non-basketball-related situations would not influence her evaluation of Cunningham.

"Sophie's had two really productive years for us in terms of shooting the basketball," Cox said. "She is a really solid leader in the locker room, a great connector. She brings levity but also brings a lot of experience. She's serious and is an important voice in our locker room when we need it. When we really need to lock in.

"She's an unrestricted free agent, so we look forward to having those conversations. Again, she had a really productive year, and we'll see just where things take us."

stories.headline: UEFA receives Real Madrid dossier on Barcelona-Negreira case
stories.summary: UEFA has received "a substantial amount of documents" from Real Madrid related to its ongoing inquiry into the Negreira case, European football's governing body said on Thursday.
stories.body:
MADRID -- UEFA has received "a substantial amount of documents" from Real Madrid related to its ongoing inquiry into the Negreira case, European football's governing body said on Thursday.

Payments made by Barcelona to companies linked to José María Enriquez Negreira -- the former vice-president of Spain's Technical Committee of Referees -- over two decades have been subject to a UEFA investigation since 2023, while there is also an ongoing Spanish criminal case.

Barcelona have said the payments, which totaled over €7 million ($7.9m), were made for technical refereeing reports.

- Ronaldo's Portugal walkout is nothing new; he has a long history of rows with coaches

- Source: Mbappé to be available for Clásico

- Raphinha back at Barça, injured in Brazil game

"UEFA can confirm that it has received from Real Madrid CF a substantial amount of documents related to the ongoing investigation into FC Barcelona in the matter involving José María Enríquez Negreira," UEFA confirmed in a statement on Thursday.

"The UEFA Ethics and Disciplinary Inspectors have also received these latest documents which they will assess as part of their ongoing review."

Real Madrid said the dossier included "extensive documentation and evidence regarding events of extraordinary seriousness, which directly affect the integrity of the competition and confidence in the refereeing system."

"Real Madrid C.F. considers it essential that, now that UEFA has this documentation, the investigation proceeds with the utmost urgency until its full conclusion, and that the competent bodies take the appropriate decisions in accordance with the severity of the verified facts," the club said.

"Our club will continue to actively collaborate with UEFA and take all actions within its power to clarify events that it deems incompatible with the principles of integrity, transparency, and fair play that should govern European football."

In May, Madrid president Florentino Pérez said that the club was gathering evidence to submit a dossier to UEFA.

Having previously adopted a conciliatory tone with Barcelona -- saying in 2024 that the two clubs "have to help each other" as they worked together on the proposed European Super League -- Pérez has since been extremely critical of his LaLiga rivals.

"They've stolen seven league [titles] from me," Pérez said in May.

In a statement, Barcelona emphasized that Thursday's development did not equate to "any new proceedings."

"The proceedings were initiated in 2023, with the appointment of two investigators who have since carried out the action they deemed appropriate," Barcelona said. "The Club has always complied with all their requests. These proceedings have not been reopened because they have never been closed.

"The UEFA statement confirms receipt of documentation submitted by Real Madrid and indicates that the investigators will assess it within the framework of the existing investigation. The same text expressly refers, on two occasions, to an investigation and a review that are 'ongoing.' It therefore does not announce the opening, reopening, or reactivation of any proceedings, nor does it contain any assessment of the substance or value of the documentation provided.

"It is up to the investigators to determine what action, if any, they consider appropriate regarding this documentation. As of today, they have not made any new requests to FC Barcelona nor have they forwarded Real Madrid's complaint to the Club. Should they do so, the Club will respond accordingly, as it has done up to now.

"In accordance with the applicable legislation governing this matter, these proceedings are subject to the outcome of the criminal case currently being heard in Spain and will continue to be so."

stories.headline: Long recovery for victims as Knights crash driver held
stories.summary: A young girl remains in hospital with serious injuries after a car careened into a crowd farewelling the Newcastle Knights ahead of the NRL grand final.
stories.body:
A young girl faces a long recovery as other Newcastle Knights supporters are released from hospital with injuries they suffered when a car ploughed into their group.

The man behind the wheel in the crash, 18-year-old P-plater Indika Bambrick Samarasinghe, was on Sunday refused bail after being charged over Saturday's incident.

A five-year-old girl was one of two patients in a serious but stable condition in hospital after previously being placed in an induced coma with critical injuries.

Another patient was in a serious condition, while four were stable and four discharged, a NSW Health spokesperson said hours before the Knights were due to take the field in the NRL grand final.

Multiple fundraisers have been established for the victims of the incident, which happened near a roundabout at Wallsend, outside Newcastle.

More than $35,000 had been raised for the wounded girl and her mother, who was also injured in the crash.

"Our family is asking for your help following a devastating incident on Link Road that has left our loved ones facing an incredibly difficult and uncertain road ahead," the girl's aunt said.

"Both mum and child now have a long road ahead of them, with ongoing surgeries, hospital stays, rehabilitation and recovery."

They were injured when Samarasinghe's BMW careered into a crowd gathered on the side of the road to farewell the Knights on their journey to Sydney for the match.

Among the group was Chris Clancy, who said there was a carnival atmosphere at the roundabout with cars beeping their horns and people waving before the disaster unfolded.

"The next thing, this car stops (at) the roundabout and then he just floored it on the wet ground, lost it," he told AAP.

"It happened in seconds, but when you stand there, seeing the car coming at you, I honestly thought I was going to die. It just felt like slow motion."

Mr Clancy suffered fractures in his ribs, spine and foot, and a broken collarbone.

Samarasinghe was taken to hospital for mandatory testing and subsequently charged with nine offences, including dangerous driving occasioning grievous bodily harm, negligent driving and causing bodily harm by misconduct.

He did not make any application for release during a brief court appearance on Sunday and was formally refused bail.

The bail court was told the most serious offence of dangerous driving occasioning grievous bodily harm carried a maximum jail term of seven years.

Samarasinghe will next appear at Newcastle Local Court on October 15.

Investigators did not believe the incident was deliberate but previously declined to comment on reports the vehicle was being driven erratically before the crash.

Dave Martin, 67, was also injured after being struck by the car while trying to protect his two young granddaughters, sustaining multiple fractures in both legs and undergoing a lengthy surgery.

He was known in Wallsend for his love of the Knights, often decorating his barber shop on Nelson St with team paraphernalia.

Knights chief executive Peter Parr expressed deep concern for those impacted by the crash.

"Newcastle is a strong community," he said.

"We have seen that strength throughout this week and today we need to draw on it again with compassion, care and support for those who need it most."

Officers are coordinating a high-visibility operation across the Newcastle and Hunter areas after the game.

NSW Police have asked the public not to congregate on major motorways as no fan engagements are planned for Sunday.
